eli5.text: When you visit the Agent Store page, you'll now see either a 'Create Publisher' button or a 'My Publishers' button in the top-right corner of the header, but only if you're signed in. The site checks your account and shows the 'Create Publisher' button if you don't have any publishers yet, or the 'My Publishers' button if you already have at least one, letting you quickly jump to manage your publishers.

ai.title: Drop initial files from first-read path in get-file-reading-updates
ai.summary: Removes `getInitialFiles` injection from `backend/src/get-file-reading-updates.ts` so first reads only surface explicitly requested or edited files. Prevents knowledge files from being included twice when `previousFileList` is empty. Scope limited to backend file-reading logic; no CLI or Web surface changes. `newFiles` now derives solely from `filteredRequestedFiles` and `requestedLoadedFiles`.

eli5.text: When the assistant reads files for the first time, it now only shows the files you specifically asked about or edited, instead of automatically including a set of pre-selected files as well. This keeps those pre-selected files from appearing twice in the same view. The change only affects the backend file-reading logic, so you won't see it on the main interface. It's live now and only relevant to internal file-reading behavior.

ai.title: Remove fileContext from getFileReadingUpdates
ai.summary: Refactor getFileReadingUpdates signature to drop ProjectFileContext parameter. Callers in run-agent-step, find-files, and read-files updated to pass messages and options directly. Internal cleanup removes unused knowledge file injection logic from backend.

eli5.text: The assistant's backend code that tracks file reading has been simplified by removing extra parameters that were being passed along but not actually needed in most cases. Instead of carrying around detailed project context information when checking files, the relevant functions now just pass the messages and specific file options directly. You wouldn't notice any change in how the assistant works, but the underlying process is now cleaner and has a bit less code doing unnecessary work.

ai.title: Remove fileupdates tool and simplify file reading logic
ai.summary: Deleted the `file_updates` tool schema and associated injection logic in `run-agent-step.ts`. Refactored `getFileReadingUpdates` to accept only requested paths, removing complex diffing against message history and token budget filtering. This simplifies the backend agent loop by eliminating automatic file change tracking in favor of explicit tool calls.

eli5.text: The assistant used to automatically check which of your files had changed since you last looked at them, comparing new changes against everything you'd read before, filtering by token limits, and deciding what to re-read on its own. Now it has stopped doing that automatic checking. When you ask it to look at a file, it reads exactly the file you named and nothing more, without trying to sneak a look at other things it thinks changed. If you used to rely on it noticing file changes between turns without being told, that behavior is gone, you now have to explicitly ask it to read the files you want it to see.

ai.title: Release 1.0.483 ships agent store UI and API metrics fixes
ai.summary: Version 1.0.483 rolls up several user-visible changes shipped since 1.0.482, primarily in the `web/` Agent Store surface and backend agent loop. The Agent Store page now renders 'Updated' badges instead of 'New', labels weekly metrics as 'Weekly spent' and 'Weekly runs', and conditionally shows 'Create Publisher' / 'My Publishers' buttons for signed-in users via the `/api/publishers` route. The `GET /api/agents` handler now returns both aggregated all-time/weekly usage metrics and per-version metrics, resolving incorrect aggregation where every version inherited the same stats; `AgentUsageMetrics` accepts a `version` prop and zero-fills missing version data. Backend file-reading logic was simplified by dropping the `file_updates` tool schema and removing automatic `getInitialFiles` injection from `backend/src/get-file-reading-updates.ts`, so first reads surface only explicitly requested or edited files. The publisher page query removed its prior `.limit(50)` cap, allowing full agent listing regardless of count. These changes align with the Freebuff Monorepo Architecture across `web/src/app/store` and `api/agents` routes, `npm-app` release packaging, and `backend/src/` file-reading
ai.evidence: The commit `7d249b55` is a release-bump commit that increments the version field in `npm-app/release/package.json` from 1.0.482 to 1.0.483. The accompanying release notes (included in the analysis) aggregate prior commits detailing changes to the agent store UI, agent store API metrics, publisher page fetch limits, and backend file-reading logic simplification.

eli5.text: This release improves the agent store where you browse and discover AI agents, making it easier to see which publishers create the most popular agents and giving you more accurate usage statistics. The agent store page now shows clearer labels like 'Weekly spent' and 'Weekly runs' instead of vague terms, and newly updated agents display an 'Updated' badge. You can now see complete statistics for each version of an agent rather than just aggregated totals, so you can compare how different versions perform. If you're a publisher, you no longer need to worry about hitting a 50-agent limit when viewing your published agents, since all of them will display. Signed-in users also get new buttons to create or manage their own publisher profiles directly from the store header. The backend agent loop was also simplified by removing automatic file change tracking in favor of explicit tool calls, making agent behavior more predictable.

ai.title: markdown-renderer loading indicator cleanup
ai.summary: Loading indicator cleanup in `npm-app/src/display/markdown-renderer.ts` reorders timer clearing before cursor reset to prevent race conditions. The indicator line clearing width increases from 10 to 20 spaces to fully wipe the `●●●` animation. This change avoids stuck indicator states and potential memory leaks during markdown rendering.

eli5.text: You may have noticed a small flicker or a leftover loading spinner when the app renders rich text with animated dots (like '●●●') at the end of a line. Behind the scenes, the app now waits to fully erase that spinner and move the cursor back to the start of the line until after it has already stopped the animation timer, which keeps the spinner from getting 'stuck' on the screen and prevents invisible background work from piling up. If you look closely, the blank line used to wipe the spinner away is now wider (longer), so it more reliably clears the animated dots regardless of how wide they spread.

eli5.text: The version label on the software was bumped to 1.0.484, which is the packaging step that makes a batch of ready-to-use edits available to you today. Among those edits, when you open an agent's detail page you will no longer see a download button, the agent store header now includes a My Publishers button, the download button on agent detail pages is hidden, the last used date is hidden in the agent store, the loading indicator shown while rendering markdown in the chat display has been cleaned up, and the initial files are dropped from the first-read path during file-reading updates. These changes affect the parts of the app you use to browse and chat with agents, and you will notice them simply by continuing to use the app after this release is installed.

ai.title: codesearch adds maxResults param, default 30
ai.summary: code_search tool gains maxResults parameter (default 30) across common params, SDK, and npm-app handlers. Previously hardcoded to 3 results in npm-app, now configurable with truncation notice `[Results limited to X of Y total matches]` when exceeded. Updated ReadDocsParams: topic now required, default max_tokens raised 10000→20000, libraryTitle description softened. SetMessagesParams.messages type relaxed to any. SpawnAgentsParams doc clarifies parallel execution semantics.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to search your codebase, it now returns up to 30 matches by default instead of 3, so you see more of the relevant lines without extra steps. If the search finds more than the limit you set, a note like "[Results limited to 10 of 42 total matches]" appears, making it clear results were trimmed. This applies to searches run locally and through the hosted agent service, and it's live today with no action needed on your end.

ai.title: Version 1.0.485 release bump
ai.summary: Freebuff 1.0.485 is a version increment over 1.0.484 with no code changes in this commit. The release bundles the code_search maxResults parameter feature added in the preceding commit, which raises the configurable result cap from 3 to 30 with a truncation notice. This release-bump commit solely updates the version string in the `npm-app/release/package.json` manifest, consistent with prior version bumps like 1.0.483 and 1.0.484.
ai.evidence: Diff changes the `version` field from `1.0.484` to `1.0.485` in `npm-app/release/package.json`, the Freebuff release packaging manifest. Version bump is a release-bump commit with no functional code or tool changes.

eli5.text: This release makes code searching smarter and gives you more control over how many results you see at once. The code search tool now lets you look through up to thirty matches by default instead of just three, and you can adjust that number to fit what you need. If there are more results available than shown, the system now clearly tells you how many it is limiting. The documentation help built into the tool got clearer topics, and you can now pull in longer passages of reference material when you need more detail. Upgrading means faster, more flexible searches without missing relevant results that might have been hidden before.

ai.title: Add debug logging to release-staging getLatestVersion
ai.summary: Added console.log statements to getLatestVersion in npm-app/release-staging/index.js. Logs statusCode, raw body, and parsed packageData for debugging. Internal change affecting release staging script only.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes script that prepares software releases now quietly prints extra details to a developer's console while it runs, showing the web request status and the package information it receives. You would notice these additional log lines appearing in the release staging tool's output, but they don't change how the release process works. This is an internal change that only affects the release staging script.

ai.title: Refactor spinner state into dedicated utility
ai.summary: Removed inline loading indicator logic from `MarkdownStreamRenderer` in favor of the shared `Spinner` utility. The `Spinner` class now supports textless frames and returns state metadata on `stop` to allow accurate resumption in `subagent-headers`. This centralizes cursor management and animation logic across display surfaces.

eli5.text: You may have noticed the loading spinner next to agent responses sometimes flickered or got stuck in a glitchy animation. The spinner now uses a single shared utility instead of each screen managing its own, so the animation stays smooth and consistent whether you see it while a response streams in or when a sub-agent header prints. If you looked, the spinner still appears while the assistant thinks, but it now correctly pauses and resumes with its previous state instead of restarting the animation from scratch.

ai.title: Nightly evals concurrency back to 10
ai.summary: Reverted --concurrency to 10 in .github/workflows/nightly-evals.yml. Restores previous throughput after temporary reduction. No user-facing changes.

eli5.text: The company restored its automated nightly testing system to run at full speed again after temporarily slowing it down. This system runs in the background every night to check that everything still works correctly, but during the slowdown it was only running a fraction of its usual tests. The change simply flips a setting back so all the tests run again at the normal rate. No customer-facing features or products were affected; this only impacts internal quality checks.

ai.title: Fix typecheck for unit tests
ai.summary: Removed obsolete loading indicator tests from npm-app/src/__tests__/markdown-renderer.test.ts to resolve typecheck failures. Applied formatting fixes including trailing whitespace removal and arrow function parentheses. Scope limited to test suite cleanup.

eli5.text: The team removed an old on-screen spinner animation test from the list of automated checks that make sure the app is working correctly. This test was no longer matching the actual on-screen spinner, which was causing the check to fail. Now the automated checks will pass again. If you looked, you would see the spinner code is still there, but the broken test for it is gone.

ai.title: Remove temp logging from release-staging
ai.summary: Removed temporary console.log statements from getLatestVersion in npm-app/release-staging/index.js. These debug logs previously printed HTTP status codes, raw response bodies, and parsed package data to stdout. This cleanup reduces noise in the staging release pipeline output.

eli5.text: While preparing a new release, the software used to print extra diagnostic details to its progress log. Those noisy debug lines, which showed server response codes and package information, have been taken out. If you watched the release process run, the output is now cleaner and less cluttered.

ai.title: Fix strreplace file edit chaining
ai.summary: Refactored `handleStrReplace` in `backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/str-replace.ts` to resolve the latest file content directly from the last promise in `fileProcessingState.promisesByPath` instead of awaiting all pending promises. This prevents race conditions where `Promise.all` would block on unrelated or failed edits, causing the tool to read stale file states or fail to apply changes. The change ensures sequential edits within a session correctly chain off the most recent successful content update.

eli5.text: When you have the assistant make several edits to the same file in a row, those edits sometimes failed to apply correctly or read an older version of the file. The system now looks only at the result of the most recent edit instead of waiting on every pending change before starting the next one. As a result, repeated edits to a file now chain together reliably and each edit sees the latest content. The fix is live today.

ai.title: Fix strreplace null check and patch generation
ai.summary: Moved null check for initialContent to top of processStrReplace, returning error immediately instead of continuing loop. Patch generation now compares initialContent to currentContent for no-op detection, replacing allPatches.length check. Single patch created from initial to final content replaces per-replacement patches.

eli5.text: The assistant now stops immediately and gives you a clear error message when a file it needs to edit does not exist, rather than silently continuing and doing nothing. It also generates a single, accurate before-and-after comparison of the file's contents instead of stitching together several partial edits, which makes its change reports easier to follow. You would notice the difference if you tried to edit a file that doesn't exist and saw a direct explanation of the problem, or if you reviewed the assistant's edit history and saw cleaner, one-step change summaries. This is live today.

ai.title: set-output schema mismatch returns tool result instead of throwing
ai.summary: set-output handler returns validation error string instead of throwing when outputSchema.parse fails. Prevents agent crash on schema mismatch by providing feedback as tool result. Affects backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/set-output.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant's reply doesn't match the expected format, it now gets a friendly error message back and keeps going, instead of crashing and stopping. You, as the person using the assistant, would notice that a mismatched response no longer breaks the session; instead the assistant gets told what went wrong and can try again.

ai.title: Add codebase commands explorer and read-only commander lite agents
ai.summary: Introduced `codebase-commands-explorer` and `read-only-commander-lite` agent definitions. `codebase-commands-explorer` uses `openai/gpt-5` to discover build/test commands with structured output. `read-only-commander-lite` uses `x-ai/grok-code-fast-1` for speedy read-only terminal execution. `read-only-commander` moved from `.agents/base2/` to `.agents/` and updated prompt wording.

eli5.text: The tool now has two new assistants available. One reads your project code to find the right build and test commands, while the other runs quick, read-only terminal queries using a faster model. These assistants were moved and renamed, with the main one shifting to a top-level folder and gaining slightly more codebase awareness. The changes are live today as part of the September 12, 2025 update.
